## What is publicly documented

::: {.case-evidence}
Southern Ute describes forestry, fuels and prescribed fire services. Its newspaper reported a CU Boulder–USFS collaboration on treatment impacts and Tribal cultural values in the Brunot Area.
:::

Sources: [Southern Ute Indian Tribe: Southern Ute Forestry Division](https://www.southernute-nsn.gov/natural-resources/forestry/); [Southern Ute Drum; Southern Ute Forestry: Fire impacts in the Brunot Area](https://www.sudrum.com/eEditions/DrumPDF/2025/SUDrum-20250502.pdf). Reviewed October 14, 2026.

## Relationship status

A CU collaboration is publicly reported; participation in this new series is not confirmed.

## A proposed question to discuss

What monitoring or synthesis would complement the existing Brunot Area collaboration and the Tribe’s own forestry questions?

This question was drafted for the prototype; it is not attributed to the Nation, organization or practitioners.

## A possible learning contribution

Support existing work and distinguish cultural values from generic fuel-reduction metrics.

## What remains context-specific

Treaty-use and ancestral-land questions may extend beyond reservation boundaries; the relevant extent must be defined with the Tribe.
